title: Eval oracle catalog and config-impact harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: After a recent configuration rollout that caused a subtle semantic degradation on a small subset of chat flows, we identified a gap: we could not reliably map small config changes to the high-level invariants we expect from user-facing models. This ticket creates an "eval oracle catalog" (a curated set of semantic-level invariants / tests tied to classes of config changes) and a config-impact harness that can auto-generate comparison pairs, run fast localized evals, and produce triage artifacts for incident followups.

Why this is different: existing smoke/regression tests focus on surface metrics (BLEU, overall accuracy, token-level diffs). The proposed work builds oracles that express expectations like "preserve citation style for knowledge responses", "avoid hallucinating personal data for persona prompts", or "maintain conservative answer when uncertainty threshold is hit" and binds them to config diffs (e.g., kv-ttl changes, batching window, quantization flags). The harness will also attach contextual traces and a failing-case classifier to minimize manual triage time.
acceptance_criteria: An oracle catalog exists as a searchable JSON/CSV with 50+ curated invariants mapped to config-change categories
A runnable harness that: generates delta-pairs (golden vs candidate), executes an eval bucket in CI or staging, and emits a triage bundle (failing examples, metric deltas, trace links)
Automated attachment of triage bundles to incident postmortems via a standardized link format
False-positive rate for failing-case classifier below 15% on a held-out seed set
Integration with alerting: when a config rollout exceeds preconfigured delta thresholds, the harness runs and posts results to the incident channel within 30 minutes
work_done: 2026-03-10: Project kickoff with PM and reliability; agreed scope and minimal viable oracle schema (semantic label, severity, config tag, example seed).
2026-03-11: Prototype delta-pair generator implemented (500-line script) that snapshots model responses pre/post config change using shadowed traffic sampling.
2026-03-12: Built initial failing-case classifier (logistic baseline) and calibrated on recent incident dataset; preliminary FPR 22%.
2026-03-13: Design review with Console team to define triage bundle schema (trace links, token-level diffs, model versions, config diff, oracle labels).
2026-03-14: Submitted draft PR for oracle catalog schema and harness README (branch: feat/eval-oracle-harness).
blockers: Need access to archived shadow traffic for two older rollouts (SRE ownership) - requested by email to SRE on 2026-03-12
Compute budget for running broader oracle suite against full canary cohort - awaiting approval from infra budget owner
We need product guidance on severity mapping for a few domain-specific oracles (legal/privacy)
test_plan: Unit tests for oracle schema validation
Synthetic harness runs in CI that compare golden vs mutated-config responses on a stable seed set (10k samples)
Calibration runs against three past incidents to measure recall/precision of the failing-case classifier
Staging rollout using 1% shadow traffic, verify triage bundle generation and alert posting
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): run harness in shadow mode for nightly config changes, produce reports to a shared channel (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (CI gating): add a fast oracle subset to CI for config PRs that touch runtime or routing (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (automated mitigation): integrate with rollout controller to block config promotion if high-severity oracle regressions exceed thresholds (policy flags; requires approvals)
retrospective: Goal: reduce mean time to triage for config-induced regressions by >=50% for medium/high incidents
Early signal: prototype reduced manual example collection time from ~4 hours to ~30 minutes for the last incident
Action items: expand catalog coverage for privacy/legal oracles, improve failing-case classifier to <15% FPR, secure budget for broader runs
